DSH LAUNCH PLANNER — issue #226 task 8.8 part (d) Pass C: THREE surviving mediums in launch-root confirmation. Branch slice-dsh-planner-d (PR #313) at HEAD 5dc0f4f3; adopt every commit. Narrow scope: R1–R3 below, nothing else.

WHERE THIS STANDS. Run dsh-launch-planner-issue-226-tas-ed4ff1bc delivered Pass C — confirm the launched root before publishing anything — plus the two landing debts (D1 independent staging observation; D2 shims staged by rename, no retry). Its chief confirmed D1, D2, the same-checkpoint root/address repair and the pre-init unreadability latch, with 104 DSH protocol tests and 24 built-driver conformance tests green. It then parked REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM on the three findings below, confirmed by source tracing. That run stays parked for the operator; this run repairs.

THE THREE, verbatim from that chief:
R1 MEDIUM security: crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs:4017-4019 skips malformed stdout before watch.settle at 4029. With firstSeq 27, a child can append assistant/message seq 28, emit non-JSON, then emit the matching init. The pre-init store observation never runs; named_the_offer becomes true and settle confirms/publishes the root, transcript and launch, then folds pre-init work. Both clean-exit and delivered-result endings bypass run_seat's unsettled guard at 5568. Valid JSON noise instead invokes the permanent pre-init refusal. Ensure malformed pre-init output cannot skip the required observation/refusal while preserving appropriate cold-path noise handling; prove both endings with synthetic-child regressions and removal evidence.
R2 MEDIUM correctness and security: adapters.rs:4266-4267 observes a fresh sibling but returns without latching refusal. After matching init, a census containing new session-9 leaves settled=false and named_the_offer=true. Removing session-9, advancing the offered session-1 from seq 27 to 28, and emitting another event allows a later settle to publish Resumed/root_session/transcript/launch despite the already observed contrary root evidence. Missing or ambiguous offered headers at 4272-4276 have the same post-init retry-through behavior. Preserve definitive contradictions for the invocation; add disappearing-sibling cases with clean-exit and delivered-result endings that prove the contradictory census was actually observed.
R3 MEDIUM security: adapters.rs:4161-4165 and 4264-4265 discard admitted file addresses and deduplicate session IDs into sets. If session-9 already exists under --old--, a fresh depth-zero session-9 under --new-- leaves that set unchanged. With exactly one offered session-1 and its sequence advanced, confirmation succeeds despite the fresh sibling. Retain sufficient storage identity/multiplicity to detect the additional session and regression-test this separate path without expanding Pass D's unrelated matrix.

THE RULE, not the three instances. All three are one defect seen three ways: confirmation is evaluated as a PREDICATE that can be re-asked until it answers yes, where D7 makes it a LATCH. Once any observation during an invocation contradicts the offered root — a line the watcher could not read before init, a fresh sibling, a missing or ambiguous offered header — the invocation is refused for good: no later observation can confirm it, whatever the store looks like by then. And the census the latch reads must be able to SEE a contradiction: it counts storage entries by address, not distinct session ids. Find every site in the watcher that returns "not yet" where the evidence already says "never", and every site that collapses identity before comparing. Fix the rule; then prove each of R1, R2 and R3 by a synthetic-child regression on BOTH endings (clean exit, delivered result file), each asserting the named refusal reason and that no root_session, transcript locator or launch row was published, and each proved by removal.

Keep cold-path noise handling as it is: a cold launch has no offered root to contradict. Keep Pass B's admission and every inherited guard.

A FACT ABOUT THIS RECIPE: its verify gate is an exec step that runs the workspace suite by the recipe's own design; no seat chooses that invocation and it is not a finding. The smith's own validation is crate-scoped and sequential.

RULES. Assert reasons, never is_err(). Diagnostics echo no option, value, model, id or path. Hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063): no Windows handling; canonicalise temp roots; errno text from the host's io::Error. GATES for the smith: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; each crate's suite on its own; openspec validate --all --strict; both bundle compiles.

OUT OF SCOPE: Pass D's composite/containment/retained-storage matrix, 9.6, 10.x, 11.x, groups 14–15, any live provider call. DO NOT TICK 8.8 or 8.10. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move; 0056 stays proposed; the DSH route stays disabled. Record what you delivered and what Pass D and 9.6 still owe.

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes: R1-R3 are implemented, proved and committed (f88535ac code, 0a76f725 tasks ledger; both signed, never pushed). Blocked on ONE smith gate only: `openspec validate --all --strict` is refused by this launch's permission grant, so it is recorded NOT RUN and 8.8.14.2/8.8.15.1 stay unticked; running that one command on 0a76f725 is all a re-run owes (only tasks.md checkbox states and a delivery section moved under openspec/ since the tasks seat's 15/0). THE RULE: confirmation is now a latch. One absorbing DshRootWatch::refuse; an immutable pre-spawn baseline (boundary, the one offered header's canonical address, every admitted (id, canonical file) occurrence) whose absence refuses in new(); one required-store rule on both sides of init (census, offered cardinality, retained address, counted sub-multiset containment, one sequence read) replacing the weaker pre-init predicate; the stream loop decodes before it observes, refuses a malformed line before init and an unreadable line while pending, and leaves cold noise handling alone. Two private seams: run_seat_with (production run_seat delegates to it, so synthetic children meet the real terminal guard) and invoke_dsh_launch_observed (per-invocation observer of each COMPLETED observation, fired on every outcome so awaits still release under removal). PROOFS: ten new synthetic-child tests; R1, R2, R3 each on clean-exit and delivered-result endings asserting the exact reason 'provider never confirmed the offered session; refusing to accept the invocation', result None, no root_session/transcript/launch/work row, one child, delivered file retained. Fourteen compiling removals (M1a, M1b, M2, M3, M4, M5, M5b, M5+M7, M6, M6', M8, M9, M10, M12) each failed its intended assertion (both endings for every contrary-evidence case; M6 fails the watcher-state assertion only, as disclosed) and were restored; restored file sha256 252cb0f7...029ef5 equals the committed one. Disclosed in the ledger: R1's headline is jointly protected (its removal is the former skip whole); removing the new() refusal changes watcher state, not the terminal reason; the post-init offered-header cardinality check is not separable from address+containment. All seven crate suites green run separately (protocol lib 407; built-driver conformance 24/24), fmt and clippy clean, both bundles compile. Exact coverage is external/pending (script also withheld here); covered/total figures unavailable.
